hints.title: Identifying Top Order Frequency
hints.text: Multiple orders originate from repeating accounts. How can transactions be partitioned to find the buyer with the peak volume?

hints.title: Order Count Descending Limit
hints.text: Group the records by customer identifier. Order the resulting groups by count descending and limit the output to one row.

hints.title: Grouped Ordering Blueprint
hints.text: Select customer_number from Orders group by customer_number order by count(*) desc limit 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT customer_number
FROM Orders
GROUP BY customer_number
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

complexity.notes: Group by customer with heap-based top-1 limit.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries counting per row waste CPU with redundant scans.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping with limit 1 avoids sorting entire customer sets when index exists on customer_number.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct aggregate ordering using count(*) desc limit 1.
